seoDescription: Learn the fundamentals of building a Svelte application by creating and styling reusable Header and Footer components. This tutorial walks you through structuring your project by organizing components into a dedicated folder, importing them into your main app file, and applying scoped CSS for a clean layout. Discover how to style the main content area for a centered column layout, manage global styles to remove default browser padding, and add a logo image to your header. This provides a solid foundation for more complex Svelte apps.

chapters.description: Creates a dedicated 'components' folder and builds the basic HTML structure for the Header component, including an image for the logo.

chapters.title: Importing the Header into the App
chapters.description: Imports the new Header component into the main App.svelte file and places it above the main content area.

chapters.title: Styling the Header Component
chapters.description: Adds scoped CSS within Header.svelte to style the background, padding, text alignment, and the logo image size.

chapters.title: Adjusting Global Styles
chapters.description: Inspects the browser to find and remove unwanted default padding from the global.css stylesheet.

chapters.title: Building and Styling the Footer Component
chapters.description: Creates, imports, and applies styles to a new Footer component to display a copyright notice at the bottom of the page.

chapters.title: Final Cleanup and Next Steps
chapters.description: Resolves a style caching issue, removes temporary placeholder content, and previews the next video on creating tabs.

summary:
## Application Layout & Structure

This video establishes the basic layout and component structure for a Svelte application.

- **Main Content Area**: The `<main>` element in `App.svelte` is styled to create a centered column for content.
  - `max-width: 960px;`
  - `margin: 40px auto;` (centers the block horizontally)

> [!TIP]
> It's a common practice to create a `components` folder (`src/components`) to organize reusable Svelte components like headers, footers, and buttons.

## Reusable Header & Footer Components

The video demonstrates creating, styling, and using two fundamental components:

1.  **`<Header />` Component**:
    - A stateless component with only a `<template>` and `<style>` block.
    - Contains a logo image placed inside an `<h1>` tag.
    - Styles are **scoped**, meaning CSS written in `Header.svelte` only applies to elements within that component.
    - The logo image is placed in the `public/image` directory and referenced via its path.

2.  **`<Footer />` Component**:
    - A simple component to display a copyright notice.
    - Styled with padding, a top border, and subtle text color to be less prominent.

To use these components, you must first **import** them into the parent component (e.g., `App.svelte`) and then place them in the template using their tag names (`<Header />`, `<Footer />`).

```javascript
// In App.svelte
import Header from './components/Header.svelte';
import Footer from './components/Footer.svelte';
```

## Global vs. Scoped Styles

The video highlights the difference between global and component-scoped styles.

- **Scoped Styles**: Styles defined inside a component's `<style>` tag are scoped by Svelte and won't leak out to affect other components.
- **Global Styles**: Styles in `public/global.css` apply to the entire application. The video shows removing default `padding` from the `body` in this file to make the header and footer flush with the page edges.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> If your styles don't seem to be updating correctly, it might be a browser caching issue. Try performing a **hard refresh** (Ctrl+Shift+R or Cmd+Shift+R) to force the browser to download the latest CSS files.

## Centering the Main Content Layout

Okay, my friends. So in this video, I just want to focus on fleshing out the header component and also the footer components at the top and the bottom of the website, essentially. But first of all, I'd like to also do a little bit inside the root component, just a tiny little bit.

So first of all, I'm going to do a paragraph tag and then just type out some lorem here. And that's just so we have something to play with on the screen. So let me save that and preview over here, and we see this paragraph going all the way from the left to the right.

Now, instead of the content spanning all the way across, I'd like to create a column of content which sits in the middle, which has a maximum width of about 960 pixels. And then the margin is auto left and right, so we have space on the left and on the right.

So to do that, I'm going to target the main tag right here, and I'm going to say that the max width will be 960 pixels. And I'm also going to say that the margin is going to be about 40 pixels top and bottom, auto left and right. If I save this now, you'll notice that the maximum width is this right here. It still looks quite wide, but that's because I'm zoomed in. If I zoom out a little bit, see it 100%, we can see now we have this central column right here, and we have a margin on the left and the right.

So that's all I wanted to do really inside this App.svelte component.

## Creating a Component Folder and Header Markup

Now then, what I'm going to do is create a new folder, and I'm going to call this `components`. I'm just going to structure my code a little more than we did in the previous tutorials. So this folder right here is going to be for our components like the footer, the header, the poll form, the poll list, etc. Now, you can structure your code differently, that's absolutely fine. This is just so we can stay organized for now. And generally in bigger projects, I would have different folders for each feature or section of the website, but in our case, that's a bit over the top, so this will do for now.

So now let's create a header component. We'll call this `Header.svelte`. And inside here, first of all, I'm going to do a script, and then at the bottom we'll have some styles. So style tag as well. And then let's flush out the template first of all. So the header itself is just going to be a `header` tag like so. And inside the header, we're going to have an `h1`. And inside the `h1`, not some text, but instead an image. And in fact, you know what, we don't even need a script because there's going to be no kind of logic or data inside this component. So let's get rid of all of that and just have the HTML template and some styles.

Now the alt attribute is going to say `poll-ninja-logo`. And we now need to add this image right here. So we're going to add that inside the public directory, and it's going to go inside a folder, so new folder called `image`. So I already have this image prepped, it's an SVG. And you can find this on the Git repo for this lesson. I'll leave the link down below. So this is the SVG preview, but you're going to see what it looks like on the screen when we add it in right here. So we want to go inside the `image` folder and then `/poll_ninja_logo.svg`.

## Importing the Header into the App

So if I save that and preview, then if we refresh... okay, we can't see that. That's because, stupidly, I've not actually imported the header component into the App component right here. So let's do that now. So, `import Header from './components/Header.svelte'`. And now we need to choose where to put this on the page. It's going to go above the main tag right here. So let's do that. `Header` like so. Save it, and now we should see that over here on the screen. Okay, so that's the logo.

## Styling the Header Component

However, looking pretty stupid and rather big. So let's now add some styles to the header. So first of all, I'm going to target the `header` tag itself. The background of this is going to be a really light gray. So that's going to be `#f7f7f7`, and it's more kind of an off-white. Now, I also want to apply some padding to this of 20 pixels all the way around.

Now let's move on to the `h1`, and the `h1` is going to have a margin of zero. So we're just stripping out the default margin of the `h1` in the browser. And then we're going to say `text-align` is going to be center. So the image is centrally aligned. Let's have a look so far. Okay, so looking a bit better. But now we need to reduce the size of this image. So I'm going to come down here and say `image`, and the max width of this image is going to be about 180 pixels. Okay, so save that and that is looking a lot better.

## Adjusting Global Styles

So I'm just going to inspect this at the minute because I can see some kind of border or margin around the body. It's the padding. So I think that's in the global style sheet. I'm going to actually remove that. So let me go to the global style sheet, which is here, `global.css`, and you can see we have some padding right here. Let's get rid of that. We don't want that. Save it, and that looks a bit better. So it now sits flush to the top, left, and right.

## Building and Styling the Footer Component

Okay, so the next thing I'd like to do is a footer component just to add a copyright notice or something down at the bottom. So let's create that. We'll get rid of the header for now. Create a new component inside the `components` folder called `Footer.svelte`. And inside here, we don't need a script again. Let's just do a `footer` tag for the template, and then a `div` with a class of `copyright`. And inside here, we're just going to say `Copyright 2020 Poll Ninja`. All right, sir.

Now let's do some styles. And before we do any styles, let's just take this component and place it inside our `App` file. So I'm going to duplicate this line and change this and this to `footer` instead. And we're going to output the footer underneath the main tag, so `footer` like so. Save it and preview, and we should see this copyright notice right here.

Now I want to centrally align that. So let's go to the styles. And I'm going to say `footer` first of all. Inside that, we'll give this some padding of around 40 pixels. I'm also going to say `text-align` is going to be center. Now I want to style this as well, `copyright`, but before we do that, let me just spell this correctly. So down here, I'm going to say `.copyright`, and then inside, the color... this is going to be kind of like a light gray instead of black just to make it a bit more subtle, so `#aaa`. And then the font size is going to be 14 pixels. The `display` is going to be `inline-block`, and the `padding` is going to be 20 pixels all the way around. And then finally a `border-top` of `1px solid` and a lightish gray color, `#ddd`. So if I save that now and preview over here, this looks a bit better.

## Final Cleanup and Next Steps

Now when we have more content in the center, it's going to look better because this will be at the bottom of the page, but for now that's looking pretty good.

But we have this padding back at the top. I don't know why that is. Oh, it's because we're loading old styles. Just hard refresh over here to get rid of that padding if it's showing up on yours. Okay then, so that is the basic template done. Now we have the header component and we also have the footer component, and we've styled the content in the middle a little bit as well.

Now we don't need that so we can get rid of the paragraph content right here. That was just so we could style it properly. Now in the next video, we're going to create some tabs for the top over here so we can switch between two different views. We have one section for showing the polls and one section for adding a new poll or form. So we're going to create some tabs in the next video to switch between two different components showing on the screen.
